example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, fixed asset register and book depreciation, September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.fixed-asset-register.xlsx: the name of the owner's register spreadsheet

messages.text: Can you update our fixed asset register for September and work out the depreciation?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need ten answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Please attach your asset register, if you have one.
What useful life, method and salvage value do you use for each class of asset?
Do you book depreciation by your own policy, or post the figure from your accountant or tax return?
What is your capitalization threshold? I never assume one.
Which rule do you use for the first month: full month, half-month or pro-rata?
Do you report under US GAAP, IFRS or local GAAP?
Did anything happen that can reduce an asset's value? When did someone last count the assets, and who?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. September. Register attached. Machinery 10 years, computers 3 years, no salvage. Vehicles 5 years, $5,000 salvage. All straight-line, by our own policy. Threshold $2,500, full month, US GAAP, US federal tax. No events. The operations manager counted in December 2023.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: No fixed-asset module is connected, so the register comes from your spreadsheet. It has six assets and the land at 31 August.
messages.after: Here is my plan. I run the register for **Northbrook Trading** for **September** under **US GAAP**. Every class is straight-line, with a **$2,500** threshold and the **full-month** rule. I calculate book depreciation only. Tax goes to your tax preparer. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: Asset cost accounts, includes $17,550 on 8 Sep
messages.summary: 7 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Your register says **$250,000** of cost at 31 August. The books say **$244,000**. I compare them both ways and keep two separate lists:

card.title: Tie-out, both ways
head: List
Cost
Asset
rows: On the register, not in the books
In the books, not on the register

messages.after: An asset that is not on the register never gets depreciation. I remove the server only if you agree.

messages.text: The machine went into service on 14 September. Its invoice from Delta Packaging Machines has three lines, but only one went to Machinery:

card.title: Shrink-wrap machine, M-03
rows: + Installation, posted to Repairs and maintenance

messages.after: Freight and installation make the machine ready for use, so Machinery is short by **$1,650**. With your full-month rule, September gets $19,200 ÷ 120 months = **$160.00**. Its book value at 30 September is $19,040.

messages.text: Two items in Repairs and maintenance are at or above your $2,500 threshold. A large repair can be a real repair, so each one is your decision:

card.title: Threshold scan
head: Vendor and date
Amount
Description
rows: Supply and install an office air conditioner

messages.after: I also checked the other way. No asset account has an item below $2,500. Is each item a repair or an asset?

messages.text: The forklift is a repair. The air conditioner is capital, machinery, in service 22 September. And yes, remove C-02.
Thank you. One more problem. On 15 September you sold the old van V-02 for $4,000. The books removed its $30,000 cost, but not its $30,000 of depreciation:
messages.after: The books show a loss of $26,000 instead. That is a $30,000 error in profit. Vehicles also shows a negative book value of $12,400.

messages.text: Your monthly entry posted $1,550 on 30 September, but it was out of date. Machinery showed an implied life of 12.1 years against your 10-year policy. That pointed at the missing machine:
messages.after: After the drafts, the implied life of machinery is 10.0 years. You own seven assets with a book value of **$161,705**. No asset has more depreciation than its cost less salvage.

messages.text: I propose four draft entries. Each one points to its evidence:

card.title: Draft entries, not posted
head: Entry
Amount
Evidence
rows: Add freight and installation to Machinery
Move the air conditioner from Repairs to Machinery, with $35 depreciation
Remove the van's depreciation. Clear the $26,000 loss and record the $4,000 gain

messages.after: The air conditioner entry credits Repairs. It never credits cash or accounts payable a second time. A person posts these entries. I do not.

messages.text: Two things stay with people. Your tax preparer works out tax depreciation, such as section 179. The last count was December 2023, about 2 years and 9 months ago. A clean tie-out does not prove that the assets exist, so the count is overdue.
messages.after: Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. The Excel file has the eleven sheets. I saved your class policies, the $2,500 threshold, the full-month rule, the account map and US GAAP.
messages.after: I never save the register, costs or book values. Next month, the run starts from your policies.
